verbalization: Curguligine B is implicated in the regulation of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1 through a series of molecular interactions. The evidence suggests that Curguligine B acts as a target for multiple compounds, including Bicyclo[7.2.0]undec-3-en-5-ol, Isopropyl caprate, and 3-Hydroxymollugin, all of which are known to interact with the DNMT3A2/3L complex. This complex, in turn, is the target of these compounds, and the DNMT3A2/3L complex is directly linked to Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential mechanism by which Curguligine B influences the transporter through its interaction with the DNMT3A2/3L complex, suggesting a broader role in modulating anion transport activity. The evidence supports a direct or indirect relationship between Curguligine B and Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1, mediated through the DNMT3A2/3L complex, and underscores the importance of targeting this pathway for therapeutic intervention.
